_about: UNC Joint Fluids Lab wave tank (Chapman Hall) and its 30-piston wavemaker. Every length in metres. Each value carries how it was obtained and how sure it is; edit a value here and everything downstream (volumes, wave model, 3D model, drawings) follows. See MEASUREMENTS.md for the working behind each number.

frame.x: along the channel axis, 0 at the channel mouth (inside face of the head's channel-side wall), positive toward the reservoir
frame.y: across the axis, 0 on the centreline
frame.z: up, 0 on the inside of the tank floor

length.how: William 28 Oct: 16 windows down each side, with beams between them alternating 4, 5, 4, ... 4 in from the head-end corner to the reservoir (15 beams, 67 in). The channel's window width is ASSUMED equal to the head's measured 39.25 in (the photos' post spacing, 1.07 m with range 1.00-1.15, agrees with the 1.11 m this implies); corners read like the head's. 16 x 39.25 + 67 + 2 x 2 3/8 = 699.75 in. Replaces the 15.4 m perspective fit of IMG_2468. Tape one channel window to settle it. Checked 7 Nov against the IIHR lab plan (sheet 1, scaled by its own dimension chain at 0.958 in per pixel): about 711 in (18.06 m) between the gate posts at the head and at the reservoir, consistent with this to within the gate frames

width.how: tape, William 28 Oct: the channel's inside width, wall to wall where the water is, 29.25 in. Replaces the 26.5 in in app/solitons.py TANK_WIDTH_MM

depth_to_rim.how: IIHR sheet 4 (typical wide and shallow basin section), also sheets 13 and 16: 5'-3 7/8" from the lab floor to the 'Max Depth' line, the rim 5" above that, and the floor 1'-11 1/2" up, so the rim is 45.4 in (1.153 m) and the maximum water depth 40.4 in (1.026 m) above the tank floor. The 42.5 in William taped is the glass window, which sits inside the frame. Only the wide basin's sections are in the archive; the channel is taken to share its rim line, as the photos show. Before 7 Nov the model took the 42.5 in window height as the rim

side_wall.corners: not measured yet: taken like the head's corner beams (2 3/8 in inner flange inside the water face)
side_wall.how: William 28 Oct: 16 windows, beams alternating 4 and 5 in starting with 4 in at the head-end corner, up to the corner where the channel meets the tall reservoir. Window width assumed from the head

frame_module.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2461/2465: post spacing from floor contact points (superseded 28 Oct by side_wall: the measured beams with the assumed 39.25 in windows)

lid_panel.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2468: spacing of the glass lid joints

head._note: The wide tank at the piston end. The channel leaves from the middle of its channel-side wall (a T, no turns). It holds the piston bank.

length_along_axis.how: tape, William 28 Oct: each long side is 8 windows of 39.25 in with 7 beams between them, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5, 4, 5 in (32 in), so 346 in between the corner beams. The corners are not measured yet; taking them like the back wall's corner beams (the inner 2 3/8 in flange inside the water face) gives 350.75 in. Replaces the 5-bay photo count (5.07 m). IIHR sheet 1 checks it: the wide basin is 4 modules (end 7'-9 1/4", two of 7'-4", gate 7'-10 1/2" = 363.75 in over the posts), and the plan scales to about 359 in

width_across.how: tape, William 28 Oct: the back face is 125 in end to end over the corner beams; inside, the water face is 125 - 2 x 2 3/8 in (outer flanges) - 2 x 1/4 in (webs) = 119.75 in

back_wall.how: William 28 Oct: three windows between four steel beams, corners included; each beam face is 5 in (2 3/8 in each side, 1/4 in between); the windows are what is left, (125 - 4 x 5) / 3 = 35 in each, assuming equal windows

side_wall.corners: not measured yet: taken like the back wall's corner beams (5 in face, 2 3/8 in inner flange inside)
side_wall.how: William 28 Oct: 8 windows a side, each 42.5 in high and 39.25 in wide end to end; the beams between them alternate 5 and 4 in, starting and ending with 5 in at the corners

depth_to_rim.how: IIHR sheet 4 (typical wide and shallow basin section), also sheets 13 and 16: 5'-3 7/8" from the lab floor to the 'Max Depth' line, the rim 5" above that, and the floor 1'-11 1/2" up, so the rim is 45.4 in (1.153 m) and the maximum water depth 40.4 in (1.026 m) above the tank floor. The 42.5 in William taped is the glass window, which sits inside the frame. Head section drawn; Before 7 Nov the model took the 42.5 in window height as the rim

max_water_depth.how: IIHR sheet 4: 'Max Depth' 5 in below the rim, 40.4 in above the floor

reservoir._note: Tall blue dam-break column at the far end, behind a gate. Modelled only as a closed (reflecting) end wall for piston waves.

length_along_axis.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2466: face length / height above rim = 3.12, height from IMG_2468

width.how: photogrammetry, IMG_2468: end face about 1.0 m outside the frame; inside assumed close to the channel

height_above_channel_floor.how: IMG_2468: top 1.8 m above the channel rim; UNC Research quotes a 'three-meter water column'

tank_floor_above_lab_floor.how: IIHR sheets 4, 13 and 16: 1'-11 1/2" (23.5 in) from the lab floor to the top of the basin floor structure. Replaces the 0.60 m photogrammetry of IMG_2465, which it confirms

piston_bank._note: 30 cylinders, 3 across the axis by 10 along it, standing on a stepped block of sheet-metal ducts in the head at the channel mouth (archive: Design/Mechanicals/Frame/FramedDucts.png, Ducts/). Each cylinder discharges through its own duct, which turns horizontal at the cylinder's bottom and runs to the block's front face, where all 30 outlets open into the channel: 3 lanes by 10 layers. William's 'row n' is one group of three along the tank; in the code that is column n (display pistons 3n-2, 3n-1, 3n).

pitch_across.how: drawn: 9.800 in. Ducts (Elbow, Extend, Extend2) are 9.8 in wide and stacked three across; the flange plate's three 8.25 in holes are on 9.8 in centres; the horizontal rails' bolt holes are 9.800 +/- .005 in apart along the tank (archive Design/Mechanicals/Ducts/RapidQuote/Mar2015/*.stp, Frame/HorizontalRails.pdf). Replaces 9.75 in (the channel width / 3), which IMG_2459 could not tell from this

pitch_along.how: drawn: 9.800 in. Ducts (Elbow, Extend, Extend2) are 9.8 in wide and stacked three across; the flange plate's three 8.25 in holes are on 9.8 in centres; the horizontal rails' bolt holes are 9.800 +/- .005 in apart along the tank (archive Design/Mechanicals/Ducts/RapidQuote/Mar2015/*.stp, Frame/HorizontalRails.pdf). Replaces 9.75 in (the channel width / 3), which IMG_2459 could not tell from this

near_end_x.how: the duct block's front face, where the outlets are. Its vertical rails bolt to the tank's gate frame at the head/channel junction (archive Frame/FrameDesignNotes, Frame/Fasteners/FastenerList), so the face is taken to be at the channel mouth

pipe_top_height.how: William, 26 Oct: the tops are level, 56 in above the tank floor (row 1's 51 in pipe on its 5 in bottom). IMG_2459 agrees: about 0.42 m of pipe stands above the rim. Not taken from the design archive: its cylinder lengths (Construction/BOM_Account.ods, Grind All, Nov 2014) belong to the outdated PVC cylinder design; William, 7 Nov: the built cylinders are metal

row_bottoms.formula: row n bottom = 5 + 3.02 (n - 1) in above the tank floor
row_bottoms.how: row 1's 5 in is William's (26 Oct, 'roughly'). The step is one duct layer of the stainless duct block: a 3.000 in box with a 0.020 in plate between layers, and bolt holes every 3.020 +/- .005 in on the front vertical rails (Ducts/RapidQuote/Mar2015/*.stp, Frame/VerticalRails.pdf). William's 3 in agrees to 0.02 in a row. Row 1 (longest pipe, lowest duct, longest duct run) is at the head end and row 10 at the channel mouth, as William confirmed on 28 Oct and as the drawn block requires (the outlets are on its tall end)

bottom_offset.how: a shift added to every row bottom, for the 'roughly' in William's numbers; `wm.py calibrate --fit gain,bottom_offset` can fit it

row_10_end.how: William, 28 Oct, and the drawings: row 10 (the shortest pipes, the top duct layer) stands at the channel end, where the block's face and outlets are. 'head' means anything only with layout 'open', as the old comparison

duct_side_walls.how: layout 'open' only. With the drawn ducts, the block is solid steel boxes below each step and its sides are closed there; above the steps the cylinders stand in open water

between_pipes_open.how: above each step the cylinders stand in open water with a free surface between them (9.8 in pitch, 8.625 in OD: 39% of the footprint)

layout.how: 'ducts' (drawn, and seen in IMG_2459: the 'stacked plates' under the cylinders are the duct layers): each piston's water reaches the channel through its duct outlet at x = 0, at its layer's height, and the block is solid below each step. 'open' is the model before 7 Nov: pipe bottoms open into a layer under the bank, roofed by the pipe bottoms. Kept as a switch for comparison only

front_units.how: drawn: each duct starts in a 19.6 in (two-pitch) elbow box, so the front row of cylinders (row 10) stands one pitch back from the face, and the block is 11 pitches (107.8 in, 2.738 m) long. Duct parts count (Ducts/RapidQuote/21Oct2014/DuctPartsCount.png): row 10's ducts are a bare elbow; each row further back adds one pitch of straight duct (Extend 9.8 in, Extend2 19.6 in)

stack._note: The duct block under the cylinders, from the 2015 design files (archive Design/Mechanicals/Ducts and Frame): stainless sheet-metal ducts and stainless rails, which IMG_2459 shows under the cylinders. Inches as drawn; the code converts. Sheet metal is 0.060 in nominal 304 stainless (Rapid Sheet Metal quote 64145, Mar 2015). The same design set drew PVC cylinders, which were not built (William, 7 Nov: the cylinders are metal), so parts that fit the cylinders, like the flange plate's holes, may differ on the machine

layer_pitch_in.how: VerticalRails.pdf: holes every 3.020 +/- .005 in; Ducts STEP: 3.000 in boxes, 0.020 in plates between layers

sheet_in.how: STEP wall planes 0.059 in apart; drawings call for 0.060 in nominal

duct_inside_in.how: 9.8 - 2 x 0.059 across; 3.0 - 0.059 from the duct floor to the top lip, which is open over the middle 8.1 in and closed by the plate and box above

flange_hole_diameter_in.how: FlangePlate.stp: three 8.25 in holes, the opening from each cylinder into its elbow. Sized for the PVC cylinders of the design (8.050 in bore); with the built 8.329 in bore it may differ. Not used in the hydraulics

outlet_band.formula: row n's outlet spans row_bottom(n) - 3.0 in to row_bottom(n) - 0.059 in
outlet_band.how: the cylinder stands on a 0.059 in flange plate on top of its layer's elbow; the elbow's floor is 3.0 in below the plate

stack.duct_length_formula: row n's duct runs (11.5 - n) pitches from its cylinder axis to the face: 0.37 m for row 10, 2.61 m for row 1

base_plate_in.how: BasPlate2/3.stp: 29.4 in wide plates, 2 and 3 pitches long, under the bottom layer (4 + 1 of them = 11 pitches)

rails.horizontal: two 304 stainless offset tees, 104.0 in long: 6.00 in flange (4.70 in of it inboard, under the block), 4.00 in web, 0.25 in thick (Frame/HRailDetail.pdf, HorizontalRails.pdf); the block's bottom layer bolts to the webs
rails.vertical: two 2 x 2 x 1/4 in 304 angles, 30.2 in tall, at the front corners, bolted to the ducts and to the gate frame (Frame/VerticalRails.pdf, VRailDetail.pdf)
rails.gussets: two 8 x 8 x 3/8 in 304 plates joining them (Frame/Gussets.pdf)
rails.pads: support pads under the rails (Frame/SupportPads.dwb, not readable here); their thickness, about 1.6 in, is inferred from row 1's 5 in bottom

motor_mount_in.how: CadFiles/MotorMount.stp (Nov 2013 design, drawn for the PVC cylinders): 9.6 in square, 0.25 in 5086-H32 aluminium, 1.25 in bore for the slider. IMG_2459 shows square plates on the cylinder tops; their size is not measured. Only the 3D model uses it

mass_kg.how: Design/Mechanicals/Mass~: 1031 kg (2274 lb) for the 2015 design, with its PVC cylinders, centre of gravity 913 mm up. Not the built machine's mass

cylinder.spec: 8 in NPS Schedule 10S welded stainless pipe, ASTM A312 TP304/304L (Felker), stencil on IMG_2458; William, 7 Nov: the cylinders are metal

length.note: per row: pipe_top_height - row bottom, about 51 in (row 1) to 24 in (row 10)

cylinder.design_history: OUTDATED, NOT USED: the 2013-15 design drew the cylinders in PVC (8 in DWV pipe; then a Grind All prototype with an 8.050 in bore, Jan 2015; Grind All lengths 24.005-51.185 in in the Nov 2014 build order; molded PVC flanges; DAPC seals sized for them). William, 7 Nov: that design was changed, and the built cylinders are metal, stainless as far as he knows, as the stencil says. Take no cylinder, flange or seal figure from those files

pistons.drive: LinMot PS01-48x360F-C stators with PL01-28x800/720 sliders, quoted with an E1200-GP-UC drive (72 V, 32 A) and a T01-72/900 supply by Scott Equipment (quote 10033082, 1 Aug 2014; sizing sheet 'UNC quote 48 300mm stroke rev3.xlsx', which sized them for 440 N at 1 Hz). The machine now runs them from an Allen-Bradley ControlLogix PLC (wavemaker-f25)

position_mm.how: app/params.py; -20 is the top of the travel, 370 the bottom; down pushes water out of the pipe (Model.py parking notes)

bestehorn_jerk_factor.how: makes the model reproduce the measured 3.834 s cycle of BIGGER WAVE.csv (0-350 mm, 500 mm/s, 10000 mm/s2, jerk 2000, Bestehorn), .claude/skills/wavemaker/SKILL.md

disc_face_at_0mm.how: ESTIMATED from the motor geometry, still to be measured. The stators stand on the 0.25 in plate on each pipe top with the slider coming out of their front face downward (IMG_2459). At drive position p the slider's front end is p + 32 mm below the stator face (data sheet stroke -25..485 mm against the drive's -57..453 mm), so at 0 mm it is about 1.39 m up, and the disc face a few cm lower. The model assumed 1.30 m before 7 Nov. Only the length of trapped air depends on it

park_mm.how: wavemaker-f25 Model.py PARK_POSITION: after a stop the pistons rest at the bottom of travel (REST_DOWN is the default), so a run starts from 370 mm and the Prepare step lifts them to Position 1

motor.how: LinMot data sheet 0185-1005 (P01-48x360F, edition 24), page 360x510. The extended stroke runs from 25 mm inside the stator's front face to 485 mm out of it; full force over the middle 360 mm (50 to 410 mm out), falling to 79% at the ends. The drive's configured envelope, -57 to 453 mm, is exactly that 510 mm, shifted 32 mm. Max speed and force are at 72 V; the drives' supply voltage on the machine is not recorded here. A fan cooler (HV01-37/48) was quoted; whether the machine has them is not known

moving_mass_kg.how: slider 3.56 kg (data sheet) plus the disc, its seal and the coupling: about 3 kg, ESTIMATED. Only the motor force check uses it

seal.value: rubber seal on the disc (William, 26 Oct); its type is not known
seal.how: The design archive's seal, a custom 8 in double-acting piston cup (DAPC-800-SP1, Smith Seal, ordered Nov 2014), was sized for the PVC cylinders, which were not built, so it says nothing about the machine's seal. Whether air gets past it ('tight' or 'leaky') is still open: bubbles or a measured wave decide it

_sources.design_archive: The 2013-2015 design files of the wavemaker (Leandra Vicci, UNC Computer Science, NSF MRI grant DMS-1229471), downloaded 7 Nov 2026 from the lab's shared Google Drive folder 'Wavemaker' to Wave_maker/Wavemaker_Drive/WaveMaker_Leah_versions (outside this repository). BLUEPRINTS.md says which files matter and what each gave.
_sources.tank_drawings: IIHR (University of Iowa) construction drawings of the 'Wave Basin and Sediment Flume', sheets 1, 4, 8, 13 and 16, dated 4-7 Jul 2009, in Design/Infrastructure/WaveTankDrawings of the archive
_sources.motor_datasheet: LinMot data sheet 0185-1005, Linear Motors P01-48x360F, edition 24 (shop.linmot.com), page P01-48x360F/360x510 for the 800 mm slider
